full_text_en:
Shen Xixian et al. (182 persons) v. Beijing Municipal Planning Commission — Dispute over Issuance of Construction Engineering Planning Permit

Ruling Summary

Pursuant to the provisions of Article 13 of the Environmental Protection Law, where a planning authority approves a project that pollutes the environment, and the applicant fails to provide an environmental impact report and the construction project does not comply with relevant national standards, the act of issuing a construction permit is illegal and shall be revoked.

Plaintiffs: Shen Xixian et al. (182 persons) (names omitted).

Litigation Representatives: Shen Xixian, resident of Building 4, Panjiayuan Nanli, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Litigation Representatives: Wang Genbao, resident of Building 6, Panjiayuan Nanli, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Litigation Representatives: Sun Jianrong, resident of Building 6, Panjiayuan Nanli, Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Defendant: Beijing Municipal Planning Commission. Address: Xicheng District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Chen Gang, Director of the Commission.

Third Party: Nutrition and Food Safety Institute of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Address: Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Wang Maoqi, Director of the Institute.

Third Party: Institute of Environmental and Health Related Product Safety of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Address: Chaoyang District, Beijing.

Legal Representative: Jin Yinlong, Director of the Institute.

The Beijing Municipal Planning Commission (hereinafter referred to as the Planning Commission), in accordance with the provisions of Article 32 of the *City Planning Law of the People's Republic of China* (hereinafter referred to as the City Planning Law), issued Construction Engineering Planning Permit No. 2001 Guijian Zi 1769 on December 10, 2001, to the former Institute of Health Supervision of the Ministry of Health (subsequently merged with other units into the Nutrition and Food Safety Institute of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, hereinafter referred to as the Food Safety Institute) and the former Institute of Environmental Monitoring of the Chinese Academy of Preventive Medicine (subsequently merged with other units into the Institute of Environmental and Health Related Product Safety of the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention, hereinafter referred to as the Health Safety Institute), authorizing the construction of a Level 2 animal laboratory at No. 7, Panjiayuan Nanli, Chaoyang District. The plaintiffs, dissatisfied with the said Construction Engineering Planning Permit, filed an administrative lawsuit with the Beijing Xicheng District People's Court.

The plaintiffs alleged: We are all residents of Buildings 4 and 6, Panjiayuan Nanli, Chaoyang District, Beijing, separated from the premises of the Third Parties by only one road. The Construction Engineering Planning Permit issued by the defendant Planning Commission to the Third Parties, the Food Safety Institute and the Health Safety Institute, for the animal laboratory construction project violated statutory procedures and did not conform to the intent of legal provisions. Projects that pollute the environment must comply with the state's regulations on environmental protection management for construction projects. The environmental impact statement for a construction project must assess the pollution and environmental impact of the project, prescribe prevention measures, be preliminarily reviewed by the competent department in charge of the project, and be submitted to the environmental protection administrative department for approval in accordance with prescribed procedures. Only after the environmental impact statement is approved may the planning department approve the design task document for the construction project. However, the Planning Commission had already issued the "Notice of Approved Design Plan" on September 11, 2000, determining the feasibility study conclusion for this project. Yet the Third Parties did not apply for environmental protection approval for the animal laboratory construction project from the Beijing Environmental Protection Bureau (hereinafter referred to as the EPB) until December 7, 2000, and the EPB did not issue a definitive approval until February 21, 2002. Since no environmental impact assessment was conducted during the feasibility study phase of this project, the defendant's approval action clearly did not comply with legal provisions. In the design plan for the animal laboratory project approved by the defendant in this case, the distance between the laboratory and the plaintiffs' residential buildings was 19.09 meters, which does not meet the requirement under National Standard GB 14925-2001 that experimental animal breeding, production, and testing facilities must be located more than 50 meters away from residential areas. Furthermore, the "Interim Regulations on the Management of Experimental Animals in the Health System" promulgated and implemented by the Ministry of Health stipulate that a building for experimental animals with a certain scale must have a sanitary isolation zone of at least 20 meters. However, there is a road between the plaintiffs' residential buildings and the animal laboratory, which clearly does not meet the concept of a sanitary isolation zone. Although the Institute of Environmental Health and Engineering of the Chinese Academy of Preventive Medicine, which undertook the environmental impact assessment for this project, possesses certain qualifications, it is subordinate to the same Chinese Academy of Preventive Medicine as the Third Parties, so the environmental impact assessment it conducted may lack impartiality. The plaintiffs requested the court to revoke the Construction Engineering Planning Permit issued by the defendant to the Third Parties.

Evidence submitted by the plaintiffs:

1. 15 photographs of the relevant animal laboratory, to show that the existing animal laboratory of the Third Parties has an impact on the surrounding residential environment and that conflicts have occurred.

2. Two investigation records: one recording 5 persons including Hou Shusen, and the other recording Jia Yanjun, to show that the existing animal laboratory of the Third Parties has an impact on the surrounding environment and that conflicts have occurred between the construction entity and surrounding residents regarding the construction of the animal laboratory.

The defendant argued: Our issuance of the Construction Engineering Planning Permit was the lawful exercise of statutory duties. The construction entity for this project had organized experts to conduct discussions and had submitted the matter to the competent industry authority for approval. The Ministry of Health issued a reply in January 2000, approving the Third Parties to construct a clean-grade animal laboratory at No. 7, Panjiayuan Nanli Courtyard, Chaoyang District. The Beijing Municipal Construction Committee issued a notice for the construction project construction plan in November 2001. Based on this, our committee issued the Construction Engineering Planning Permit to the Third Parties in December 2001. Regarding the environmental protection issues of the approved project in this case, aside from the relevant reply from the Ministry of Health prior to our issuance of the planning permit, after the issuance of the planning permit, the EPB also issued the "Reply on the Environmental Impact Report Form for the Animal House Project of the Food Hygiene Inspection Institute of the Ministry of Health" in February 2002. The above circumstances indicate that the project passed the approval of relevant specialized administrative departments. The current planning approval procedure does not require the opinion of the environmental protection department as a prerequisite condition; the plaintiffs' assertion that the project must obtain consent from the environmental protection department before the Construction Engineering Planning Permit can be issued has no legal basis. Additionally, at the time our committee approved this construction project, the relevant national standards had not yet been formally implemented, and therefore they are not applicable to this case.

Evidence submitted by the defendant:

1. Reply No. [2000] 24 of the Ministry of Health on Financial and Planning Matters, to show that this project was special, that the defendant conducted extensive preliminary work, and that the project was approved by the Ministry of Health.

2. Notice No. [2001] 478 of the Beijing Municipal Construction Committee for the Construction Project Construction Plan, to show that the project was included in the 2001 annual construction plan upon review and approval by the Beijing Municipal Construction Committee.

The Third Parties, the Food Safety Institute and the Health Safety Institute, did not submit any written statements. The Food Safety Institute submitted relevant evidence during the court hearing, while the Health Safety Institute submitted no evidence.

Evidence submitted by the Third Party, the Food Safety Institute:

1. Reply No. Jing Huan Bao Jian Du Shen Zi [2002] 41 of the Beijing Environmental Protection Bureau, "Reply on the Environmental Impact Report Form for the Experimental Animal House Project of the Food Hygiene Inspection Institute of the Ministry of Health," to show that the construction project had been approved by the environmental protection department.

2. Construction Engineering Construction Permit No. 05 (Jian) 2002-2090 issued by the Beijing Municipal Construction Committee, to show that its construction was lawful.

Legal bases submitted by both the plaintiffs and the defendant:

1. Article 32 of the *City Planning Law of the People's Republic of China*: For the construction, extension, and renovation of buildings, structures, roads, pipelines, and other engineering facilities within a planned urban area, the relevant approval documents must be submitted to the competent department of urban planning for an application; the competent department of urban planning shall, based on the planning and design requirements proposed by the urban plan, issue a construction engineering planning permit.

2. Article 13 of the *Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China*: "Projects that pollute the environment must comply with the state's regulations on environmental protection management for construction projects. The environmental impact statement for a construction project must assess the pollution and environmental impact of the project, prescribe prevention measures, be preliminarily reviewed by the competent department in charge of the project, and be submitted to the environmental protection administrative department for approval in accordance with prescribed procedures. Only after the environmental impact statement is approved may the planning department approve the design task document for the construction project."

3. Article 5, Item 5 of the "Interim Regulations on the Management of Experimental Animals in the Health System" promulgated and implemented by the Ministry of Health on November 28, 1983: "A building for experimental animals with a certain scale must have a sanitary isolation zone of at least 20 meters."

4. Article 41.4 of National Standard GB 14925-2001 of the People's Republic of China, "Environmental and Housing Facilities for Laboratory Animals" (promulgated on August 29, 2001, effective on May 1, 2002): "Experimental animal breeding, production, and testing facilities shall be located more than 50 meters away from residential areas."

During the court's cross-examination, the plaintiffs did not object to the authenticity of the defendant's Evidence 1, but argued that this evidence only showed that the Ministry of Health approved funding for the Third Parties to construct the project, and did not show that the defendant considered the project's impact on the surrounding environment when approving it. The court found that this evidence only proved that the Ministry of Health approved the Third Parties to construct the project, as well as matters such as the construction location, total investment, and construction period. The plaintiffs did not object to the authenticity of the defendant's Evidence 2, but argued that it had no necessary connection to the defendant's approval action.

The defendant objected to the plaintiffs' Evidence 1, arguing that it was impossible to determine who threw the animal carcasses and from where, and that this occurred after the Planning Commission's approval and could not support the plaintiffs' claims. The Third Party, the Health Safety Institute, did not object to the authenticity of these photographs, but argued that constructing the animal laboratory was necessary. The Third Party, the Food Safety Institute, acknowledged the authenticity of these photographs, but argued that the institute had already stopped the practice of indiscriminately discarding animal carcasses, and that this evidence had little relevance to the Planning Commission's approval action. The defendant did not object to the authenticity of the plaintiffs' Evidence 2, but argued that although the animal laboratory would have an impact on the surrounding environment, this impact was a separate matter from whether the construction project could be built. Both Third Parties argued that Evidence 2 could not demonstrate that the construction project could not be built because of its impact on the surroundings.

The plaintiffs argued that the Third Parties' Evidence 1 should have been produced before the defendant's approval; the approval issued after the approval action could not demonstrate that the defendant's approval was lawful. The defendant argued that the plaintiffs' claim had no legal basis.

The Beijing Xicheng District People's Court found the following after trial:

On December 10, 2001, the defendant Planning Commission issued Construction Engineering Planning Permit No. 2001 Guijian Zi 1769 to the Third Parties, the Food Safety Institute and the Health Safety Institute. The permit indicated that the construction project was a Level 2 animal laboratory, located at No. 7, Panjiayuan Nanli, Chaoyang District, with a construction scale of 2,949.18 square meters. The appendix to the permit indicated that the Level 2 animal laboratory was to have 3 floors above ground and 1 underground floor, with a frame structure. The plaintiffs' residential buildings were located to the north of the Level 2 animal laboratory, with Building 6 being 19.06 meters away from the planned building.

The Beijing Xicheng District People's Court held:

According to the City Planning Law, for the construction, extension, and renovation of buildings, structures, roads, pipelines, and other engineering facilities within a planned urban area, the relevant approval documents must be submitted to the competent department of urban planning for an application; the competent department of urban planning shall, based on the planning and design requirements proposed by the urban plan, issue a construction engineering planning permit. As the competent department of urban planning, the defendant has the authority to issue Construction Engineering Planning Permits for construction projects that comply with the urban planning and design requirements, upon application by the construction entity.

According to the provisions of Article 13 of the *Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China*, projects that pollute the environment must comply with the state's regulations on environmental protection management for construction projects. The environmental impact statement for a construction project must assess the pollution and environmental impact of the project, prescribe prevention measures, be preliminarily reviewed by the competent department in charge of the project, and be submitted to the environmental protection administrative department for approval in accordance with prescribed procedures. Only after the environmental impact statement is approved may the planning department approve the design task document for the construction project. When approving the Construction Engineering Planning Permit for this project, the defendant Planning Commission should have examined whether the Third Parties had obtained an environmental impact statement and, in accordance with the provisions of the "Interim Regulations on the Management of Experimental Animals in the Health System" promulgated by the Ministry of Health, examined whether the proposed experimental animal building reserved a sanitary isolation zone of at least 20 meters. However, in this case, the distance between the animal laboratory approved by the Planning Commission in the design plan and the plaintiffs' residential buildings was 19.06 meters, failing to meet the prescribed distance requirement. The evidence submitted by the Planning Commission to the court during litigation was insufficient to prove that its approval action was based on clear facts and that the procedure was proper and lawful.

Accordingly, the Beijing Xicheng District People's Court, pursuant to the provisions of Article 54(2)(1) of the *Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, on June 19, 2003, rendered judgment:

Revoke Construction Engineering Planning Permit No. 2001 Guijian Zi 1769 issued by the defendant Beijing Municipal Planning Commission to the Third Parties on December 10, 2001.

After the judgment was pronounced, the Planning Commission, dissatisfied, appealed to the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court.

The main grounds of appeal by the Planning Commission were: (1) According to the City Planning Law and the Environmental Protection Law, the duties of the Municipal Planning Commission are limited to examining whether the construction entity has obtained the approval documents from the planning department; as long as the construction entity holds the documents approved by the planning department, it can only be presumed that the prerequisites for that approval, including the "environmental impact statement," have been resolved. The Planning Commission should not examine matters that should be reviewed by other departments. (2) Regarding the issue of the "20-meter sanitary isolation zone," due to the special nature of this project, the construction entity submitted it to the Ministry of Health for review, and the Ministry of Health approved the design. This approval document is a prerequisite for the construction department to issue the planning permit; the Planning Commission need not examine this matter. (3) The first-instance judgment's finding that the Planning Commission provided insufficient evidence has no legal basis.

During the second-instance proceedings, the Planning Commission, upon reconsideration, indicated its willingness to abide by the first-instance judgment and voluntarily applied to withdraw its appeal.

The Beijing First Intermediate People's Court held:

The Planning Commission's voluntary application to withdraw its appeal during the appeal period is an act of lawfully disposing of its litigation rights. This act does not infringe upon the lawful rights of the state, collectives, or individuals, and should be granted.

Accordingly, the Beijing First Intermediate People's Court, pursuant to the provisions of Article 51 of the *Administrative Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China*, on October 24, 2003, ruled:

Grant the appellant Beijing Municipal Planning Commission's withdrawal of its appeal; the parties shall execute the first-instance judgment.
